title: Window Functions: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Collapse Or Attach | the same five ranked_results rows under GROUP BY query_id and under AVG(score) OVER (PARTITION BY query_id), input beside output | PARTITION BY divides rows the way GROUP BY does but does not change the grain, so the score and the document that produced it stay on one row

2. Three Ways To Rank | four documents with two tied at 90, numbered by ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK, with a tie-breaker toggle and a re-run button | the three functions differ only at ties, ROW_NUMBER needs a full tie-breaker or it drifts, and an arbitrary tie-breaker destroys the tie RANK exists for

3. The Frame Window | seven timed latency rows with three selectable frames, tap a row to light up the rows its answer reads | the frame decides which ordered rows feed each answer, early rows just use a smaller frame, and SQL never invents missing predecessors

4. ROWS vs RANGE | five events where pairs share a timestamp, running totals recomputed under a ROWS frame and a peer-inclusive RANGE frame | ROWS answers through this physical event and RANGE answers through this ordering value, and the usual engine default is RANGE

5. Defining Previous | daily error rates with Tuesday missing, LAG shown on the raw table and on the same data left-joined to a calendar | LAG returns the previous row rather than the previous day, so a gap in the data silently produces a two-day change reported as one
